authoring_rationale: Class C: permission and boundary crossing, engaged; Part D condition (a). Both variants carry the same rule: the digest arrives at the supporter account only when the member has switched Sharing on, and the supporter account cannot change the member's choice. One variant also states the member's current choice (Sharing on, set at first setup), so the digest arrives. The other states no current choice at all. Whether the digest currently crosses to the supporter account under the second variant cannot be determined from its text, so neither a difference nor an equivalence of the permission state can be established. Insufficiency locatable as the absent current-choice line. A delta answer would require assuming the unstated choice is off and an equivalence answer would require assuming it is on; either imports evidence the reviewer does not lawfully have. Format varied (bullets versus prose) so that form tracks nothing. Authored fresh from the public ADR-0054 and ADR-0055 law only; not adapted from or templated on any other case or corpus; no void-attempt material used. Orientation and identity computed mechanically from the final bytes (ADR-0055 decisions 7, 8 and 11); no wording was adjusted for orientation, identity or position.
